titleEn: In a Boat, Life Jacket First!

pages.text: "Let's go fishing!" Pongi hopped into the boat tied by the water. Dad, in his overalls, followed with an oar and two life jackets. The boat was still tied up, rocking in its place.
"Now, life jacket first." Dad offered the little jacket. Pongi twisted away. "I can't swim in a jacket! I won't wear it!" She pushed it aside and only looked into the water.
Dad untied the rope and rowed. The boat glided out onto the water. Then a big milk boat tooted past, sending a wave their way. Rock! The life jacket slipped over the side.
"Oh! My jacket!" Pongi gripped the side of the boat. Dad put down the oar and watched it. Their boat floated still. The jacket didn't sink. It bobbed on the water.

Dad pointed. "Look. A life jacket floats on the water like that. The middle of the canal has a strong current. Even a good swimmer might not get back to the boat." Pongi stared at the floating jacket.
Dad fished the jacket out with the oar. "Shall we play captains? A real captain puts on a life jacket first. In a boat, life jacket first!" Pongi's mouth turned up a little. "A captain?"

Dad counted on his fingers, one at a time. "One, jacket on before getting aboard! Two, tie the front straps tight! Three, when it's all on, call, 'Let's go!'" Pongi clenched her paws and lifted her chin. "I want to be captain!"
Pongi slipped her paws into the jacket and pulled the front straps tight. "Dad, I'm ready! Let's go!" She thumped her tail on the boat floor. Dad rowed, and the boat glided forward again.
The boat glided back to the bank. Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper in boots, waved his wings. "You've put your jacket on well!" Pongi called, "One, jacket on! Two, straps tight! Three, let's go!"
At home, Dad hugged Pongi tight. "You're a real little captain, Pongi!" A life jacket doesn't stop her swimming. It helps her float in the water. Pongi smiled. "In a boat, life jacket first!"
